title: Step around the blocking king
objective: Move your king around Black's king to help your pawn.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original instructional text and synthetic king-and-pawn position

steps.explanation: Black's king blocks the pawn. White's king should step around it before pushing.
steps.detail: Move your king to d5 or f5 to go around Black's king. Then your pawn can move forward with help from your king.

question.prompt: Step around Black's king, then advance the pawn.
hints: Move the king sideways to d5 or f5.

tree.feedback: Kd5 outflanks the blocking king on the queenside.

children.feedback: Black follows. Now the pawn has room to advance.
e5 advances with the king actively supporting it.
Black follows to f7. Advance the pawn.
e5 keeps the pawn protected and gains space.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may change the technique. This exercise practises outflanking before the pawn push.

takeaway: In king-and-pawn endings, use the king first. Outflank the defender, then advance the protected pawn.
